subject: ventures/ghost-kitchen-brand-picker
professional: a restaurant operations consultant who runs delivery-only kitchens and costs menus and labour for multi-brand operators

evidence.correctness: Ran analyze() on the 7-brand example and recomputed per-order profit (6.86), monthly profit (5,249.43) and break-even by hand; an independent Fraction brute-force in Python agreed with calc.mjs on 300 random instances for both the base case and the 0.7/1.3 volume cases (0 mismatches). Not 4: the labour model is simplified and a garbage packaging value is accepted silently.
evidence.completeness: Every README feature was exercised through calc.mjs (14-brand cap, per-brand profit per order/hour/break-even, four greedy rules, 25/50/100% more hours, +-30% orders, CSV with dropped list). The browser UI was not driven by a real browser here, only its source and tests read.
evidence.verification: node --test: 25 pass. Ten hand-seeded mutations on a scratch copy: 3 caught (labour divisor, break-even weeks, hours divisor), 6 survived (WEEKS_PER_MONTH=4, exact-fit boundary, margin rule, extra-hours gain, +30%->+20%, CSV minus guard), 1 equivalent. The tests check structure and invariants, not dollar values.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (10 KB), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs and index.html render code. Clean pure functions, CSV formula-injection guard, caps on inputs. Defects: silent 0 for packaging/fixed, EPS tolerance in two places, a page test that depends on repo layout (fails when the folder is copied).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty, privacy and 'Not decided' are on the page and README; the served page, llms.txt, sitemap.xml and canonical at marisstella.app are all correct after the build rewrite (curl). 'Every combination checked exactly' is backed by solve() and a 300-case independent match. No reviews or unbacked numbers.
evidence.fitness: An operator can type 7 brands and get which to keep, why the rest are dropped, rule comparison and a CSV in one pass; the stated limits (independence, no cannibalisation) are on the page. They would still need to adjust labour by hand.
evidence.domain: Compared with how operators cost labour and kitchen capacity: paying only for prep minutes and treating total prep minutes as the capacity limit ignores minimum staffing, overlapping cooking and platform fees on a tax-inclusive subtotal. Knapsack framing is sound and the 25-30% fee stack is realistic.

defects.what: Core constants and outputs are unpinned: changing WEEKS_PER_MONTH to 4, the exact-fit hour boundary, the margin-rule sort, the extra-hours gain, the +30% scale and the CSV minus guard all leave 25 tests green (6 of 9 non-equivalent seeded bugs survived). No test compares a monthly dollar figure to a hand value.

Labour is charged on prep minutes only and capacity is the sum of prep minutes at 100% utilisation. Staffed hours are paid regardless of load and a line cooks several orders at once, so absolute profits and the hour budget are optimistic; the page notes 'every hour interchangeable' but not this.
Blank or non-numeric packaging and monthly cost silently become 0 with no warning, and a blank monthly cost shows break-even 0.
Source sitemap.xml, robots.txt and canonical use relative './' URLs, but the build rewrites them and the served files are correct.

recommended_fixes: Add tests pinning the example's monthly profit (9,026.67), 52/12 weeks, an exact-fit hours case and the 1.3 scale label.
Warn when packaging or monthly cost is non-numeric.
Add a labour-model note (staffed hours vs prep minutes) to 'Not decided'.
verdict: Finished and arithmetically correct: the exact knapsack matches an independent brute force on 300 random cases and by-hand figures on the example. It does not meet the bar because verification is 2: 6 of 9 non-equivalent seeded bugs survive 25 passing tests, including a wrong weeks-per-month constant, and the labour/capacity model (domain 2) is simpler than an operator's real cost. Fixing the tests is a few lines.
